change: 1) Replaced 'abs' secondary (Upper/Lower Rectus Abdominis) with 'oblique' (External Obliques + Internal Obliques): unilateral exercise per CLAUDE.md rules requires anti-rotation oblique engagement, not generic abs. 2) Added Gluteus Medius to the primary glutes entry: EMG studies (2024 descriptive EMG study, PLOS One lunge EMG) confirm meaningful gluteus medius activation during reverse lunge for hip abduction stability.

Moved Upper Traps and Lower Traps from primary mid back to secondary mid back. For a rowing movement, the prime movers are Latissimus Dorsi and Rhomboids (scapular retraction and shoulder extension). Upper and lower trapezius act as scapular stabilizers/rotators (secondary), not primary movers. Split the original merged primary mid back entry into: primary = Rhomboids only; secondary mid back = Upper Traps + Lower Traps. Removed Lower Back (Erector Spinae) from secondary — with one knee and hand supported on bench, erector spinae demand is minimal and not meaningfully engaged. This opened a slot for the corrected traps entry.

Removed gastrocnemius (Gastrocnemius Medial + Gastrocnemius Lateral) from secondary. With knees bent at ~90 degrees, the gastrocnemius is in active insufficiency (it crosses both knee and ankle joints); biomechanics research confirms it cannot contribute meaningfully in the seated position. The exercise is a soleus isolation — secondary is now empty.

No changes. Primary Lats (Latissimus Dorsi) + shoulders (Posterior Deltoid) correctly reflects shoulder extension biomechanics (lats are primary mover; posterior deltoid is synergist). Secondary Triceps Brachii (long head assists extension) and mid back Rhomboids (scapular stabilizer) are appropriate. Teres Major is a known synergist but has no allowed bucket/latin term in the system, so correctly omitted.

No changes. Primary Upper Traps is correct for the shoulder elevation action. Secondary mid back (Rhomboids + Lower Traps as scapular stabilizers), forearms (Wrist Flexors for grip), and Lower Back (Erector Spinae for isometric postural hold) are all well-supported. Levator scapulae is a known synergist but has no allowed mapping in the system.
